2-Step Agent documentation

This package provides tools for Bayesian agent modeling and structural causal models (SCM).

Agent Model

Better name: bayesian_agent? -Could initialize with an SCM that represents the

agent’s internal representation of the world.

-Class could store the trace and perhaps using this

model the predictions based on the SCM.

-This would make the class contain both the agent’s

beliefs and thought processes (how to update beliefs based on new data).

The Bayesian models specified here correspond to how an ideal Bayesian agent would update his beliefs given that he sees one or several observations and receives their predictions that are based on an OLS regression model without intercept.

The agent is considered to have a separate SCM which uses the agent’s (prior or posterior) beliefs to choose the best treatment for a patient.

Technically only one value of X should be allowed after update. -Is there any point of allowing for sampling for other X-values? -The model is NOT VALID for other X values. -Don’t block this (yet), because that would prevent updating with

e.g. 100 patients’ info.

Could be interesting to estimate variance for CATE using sampling as we should expect correlation between E(Y|X,do(A1)) and E(Y|X,do(A0)) but do not know how large that is. This applies to both prior and posterior.

This method generates a sample from the agent’s posterior beliefs. Using the trace stored in self, this method replaces the parameter values in self.predictive_scm and draws a posterior predictive sample from this.

Structural Causal Model (SCM)

Structural causal model (SCM) for -data generation, and -for agent’s internal representation. Agent uses this model to prescribe treatment based on his prior beliefs before seeing new information, and based on his posterior beliefs after seeing new information.

Notes: Might be more efficient to reimplement the SCM class using pymc, especially as the Bayesian agent (agent model) is implemented using pymc.

get_CATE_mu(A1_fixed, A0_fixed)

This method returns the mean of the CATE-distribution given X, A1_fixed, and A0_fixed. Due to how the SCM is defined, this value is equivalent to (A1_fixed - A0_fixed) * self.N_E.

The SCM in this class is defined so that Y given A and X is normally distributed and its parameters are deterministically determined by the values of A and X. This results in the CATE- distibution also being normal and allows for deterministic calculation of the mean as:

CATE_mu(X) = E(Y| X, do(A=A1)) - E(Y| X, do(A=A0))

Args: A1_fixed [float]: Dosage value of higher dose treatment A0_fixed [float]: Dosage value of lower dose treatment

sample(X=None, A=None, draws=1, rng=None)

This method encodes the structure of the SCM and generates samples of X, Y and A:

X, A, Y ~ p(X, Y, A).

If X is passed, then the output A and Y are conditional on the value of X:

A, Y ~ p(A, Y| X).

If A is passed, the output Y is conditional on the intervention do(A):

X, Y ~ p(X, Y| do(A)).

If both X and Y are passed, the output is conditional on X and on the intervention do(A):

Y ~ p(Y| X, do(A)).

All of X, A, and Y are always passed. In addition, the distribution parameters for Y (mu_Y_cond, and var_Y_cond) are passed. If X and/or A are provided, the distribution parameters are conditional on the given values. Otherwise they are “conditional” only on the sampled values (in contrast how the word “conditional” is normally used).

Args: X: Optional input. If provided, output will be conditional on X. A: Optional input. If provided, output will be conditional on do(A). draws (int): Size of sample to generate. rng: seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility

sample_CATE(X, A1_fixed, A0_fixed, draws=1, rng=None)

This method samples the CATE-distribution using treatment 1 (higher dosage) instead of treatment 0. Given X and two treatment options A1_fixed and A0_fixed

Args: X (float): Feature to condition on A1_fixed [float]: Dosage value of higher dose treatment A0_fixed [float]: Dosage value of lower dose treatment draws (int): Size of sample to generate rng: seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility

sample_do_A(A_fixed, X: numpy.ndarray, draws: int = 1, rng=None) → numpy.ndarray
Generates sample from the SCM given the data and set treatments, i.e.

Y_i ~ p(Y|do(A_fixed), X)

Returns an array with shape (n, *X.shape). This is merely a wrapper for the interventional path in self.sample().

Args: A_fixed (int- or array-like): value to intervene on A, or array with X.shape X: observed values of X draws (int): Size of sample to draw for every observation in A. rng: seed or initialized random number generator for reproducibility
